show.title: La Señal — Español por input comprensible
show.description: A serialized sci-fi political drama in Colombian and Venezuelan Spanish, engineered as a 365-day comprehensible-input curriculum. A Bogotá astronomer detects a signal that is not from Earth — and the fight over what it means begins. Starts slow and scaffolded, ends at full native speed. Voice references: OpenSLR SLR72/SLR75 (CC-BY-SA 4.0, © Google). Private listening feed.
show.author: La Señal

episodes.title: Episodio 0 — Prueba de nivel
episodes.description: A 12-minute listening diagnostic. Five passages, each faster and denser than the last, each followed by three spoken questions. Score yourself with the sheet in the show notes; your result sets Day 1. Instructions in English; everything else in Spanish.

episodes.title: Día 1 — «El ruido»
episodes.description: Astronomer Camila Rey works alone at night in a small observatory above Bogotá — until, at 3:47 in the morning, her computers record a noise that should not exist. Plus: what a radio telescope actually does (hint: it hears nothing).

episodes.title: Día 2 — «La rutina»
episodes.description: Camila's upside-down life: sleep by day, empanadas at doña Marta's, night shift at the dish. She replays the recording and sees something new — and her colleague Julio has one word for it. Plus: why astronomers work at night.

episodes.title: Día 3 — «El taxi»
episodes.description: Meet El Flaco: taxi driver, conspiracy podcaster, and the fastest mouth in Bogotá. Camila half-listens to his wild theories — until one sentence about the sky makes her stop smiling. Plus: why Bogotá is cold on the equator.

episodes.title: Día 4 — «Otra vez»
episodes.description: Night shift at the observatory. Camila watches the clock crawl toward 3:47 — and the sky keeps its appointment. Two occurrences is not chance. Plus: coincidence versus pattern, or how scientists decide what is real.

episodes.title: Día 5 — «El jefe»
episodes.description: Camila takes the pattern to her director and gets six words she will never forget: we need funds, not ghosts. On the ride home, for once, she is the one asking the taxi driver questions. Plus: who actually pays for astronomy.

episodes.title: La tormenta
episodes.description: A violent storm hits the hills above Bogotá, and the observatory pays the price. If the signal returns at 3:47, will anyone be listening?

episodes.title: El venezolano
episodes.description: The repair company sends an engineer to fix the storm damage. He arrives with a toolbox, a thermos he guards with his life, and opinions about arepas. Nothing at the observatory will be the same.

episodes.title: Manos a la obra
episodes.description: Two days of repairs, one story told in pieces: Caracas, the blackouts, and the long road to a hill outside Bogotá. Then Andrés asks the one question nobody else thought to ask.
The dish is fixed, the coffee is hot, and three people wait in the dark for 3:47 AM. What happens next is five minutes late — and it changes everything.

episodes.title: La apuesta
episodes.description: Over breakfast at doña Marta's, two theories about the late signal collide — and turn into a bet with national cuisine at stake. Meanwhile, director Sarmiento has heard about the engineer's extra hours.

episodes.title: Doña Marta
episodes.description: Doña Marta's food stall feeds the observatory — and hears everything on the hill. Today her gossip is funny, until she mentions two strangers in a grey SUV who were asking about Camila.

episodes.title: El favor
episodes.description: To rule out satellites, Andrés needs a favor from his old CANTV friend — and in Maracaibo, everything goes through Tía Chela. Her first voice note is four and a half minutes of family news with a bombshell buried at the end.

episodes.title: Las explicaciones
episodes.description: Camila and Andrés list every boring explanation for the signal — satellites, planes, radar, a broken sensor — and design a test for each one. Andrés insists on adding a microwave oven to the list, and promises the strangest true story in radio astronomy tomorrow.

episodes.title: Los perytones
episodes.description: Over breakfast, Andrés tells the true story of the Parkes 'perytons': seventeen years of mysterious signals that turned out to be the observatory microwave. Everyone laughs — until they remember their own signal already passed every test the perytons failed. Then Sarmiento calls: Bogotá wants the routine report early.

episodes.title: El informe
episodes.description: Sarmiento wants one safe line in the report: 'unidentified interference'. Camila writes the truth instead — and in a Bogotá office with a view, someone reads it, underlines it, and reaches for a stamp. Mundo Real: a gentle comic essay on Latin American paperwork.

episodes.title: La visita
episodes.description: Two ministry officials arrive for a 'routine' inspection, and Andrés delivers the performance of his life. Plus: how to tell a rolo from a paisa from a costeño by ear.

episodes.title: La Verdad Oculta
episodes.description: El Flaco's conspiracy podcast connects dots that were never supposed to be connected, and Camila has to make a deal. Plus: how to enjoy a wild theory without falling for one.

episodes.title: El eco
episodes.description: Andrés's new receiver hears the signal twice — once loud, once faint — and the difference between a bounce and an answer suddenly matters a great deal. Plus: whales, submarines, and the science of echoes.

episodes.title: Los radioaficionados
episodes.description: To locate the echo they need antennas they don't have, so Andrés calls on Colombia's ham-radio community — retirees, a nun, and a llanero named don Ramiro who trusts no one. Plus: the hundred-year-old internet.

episodes.title: La triangulación
episodes.description: Three antennas, one 3:47, and a dog named Rayo: the night the volunteer network listens together. Plus: how three friends shouting in a plaza explain how your phone knows where you are.

episodes.title: Demasiado cerca
episodes.description: The triangulation math is verified again and again, and the answer refuses to change: the source is inside the solar system, maybe closer than the Moon. Julio finally believes Camila — which is exactly why he wants out.

episodes.title: El hermano de Julio
episodes.description: A friendly ministry analyst just happens to drop by doña Marta's stall, and lunch turns into a polite duel where nobody says a single true thing. Afterward, Julio has something to confess.

episodes.title: La nota de voz
episodes.description: Tía Chela sends the longest voice note in Maracaibo history: three minutes of neighborhood saga with a bomb buried at minute two. Suddenly Andrés's work permit is not just paperwork anymore.

episodes.title: La decisión de Andrés
episodes.description: At dawn on the observatory roof, Andrés finally tells Camila about Caracas: the lab he lost, the team that scattered, and the antenna his father built on their roof. Then he gives her his answer.
